You are shown a snapshot of US macroeconomic and market data as it was known at the end of one month between 2007 and 2026.

Estimate which month the snapshot describes. Use only the figures supplied plus your general knowledge of economic history.

Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"year": yyyy, "month": m, "confidence": c, "cues": ["...", "..."]}
Rules: year is an integer from 2007 to 2026; month is an integer from 1 to 12; c in [0, 1] is your confidence that the guess is within 6 months of the truth; 1 to 3 short cues citing the inputs.
text:
This looks like mid-2020 to early 2021, with unemployment elevated (+2.5 z) and still rising over 3 months (+2.0), and payrolls recovering (3m change +2.5). Industrial production is deeply negative. Headline CPI is very low, and the Baa spread has narrowed sharply (-2.5 over 3m), which fits a recovery from the March 2020 spike.

Candidate months are June to September 2020, but several cues point elsewhere. The 10-year yield is up +2.0 over 3m, and Treasuries have fallen over 6m (-2.5 to -3.0), which suggests a rise in yields from the August 2020 lows. That fits a date around early 2021. Yet the unemployment rate z-score of +2.5 with a +2.0 3m change implies the rate rose recently, which fits April–May 2020 more than 2021.

Consider the alternatives. In 2020 the policy rate z would be about -1.5 against the prior 3 years (rates were 2%, then 0), which fits. The 12m equity return of -1.0 is odd for 2020 unless the date is March–April 2020, but the VIX at 0 and a Baa spread change of -2.5 rule that out.

Another candidate is late 2009 or early 2010, but the 36-month window would then include 2007 rates of 5%, giving a more extreme policy-rate z-score. Treasuries down 6m with a 10-year yield up 2.0 on 3m suggests a yield rise. In 2009, 10-year yields rose from December 2008 to June 2009, with the Baa spread narrowing sharply and equities rallying 3m (+1.5). Equity 12m is -1.0 at roughly June 2009. Headline CPI z-score at -2.0 fits mid-2009 (negative inflation). Unemployment rose sharply (+2.5), and payrolls are still negative but improving, which fits. VIX had fallen from its peak to about 0 z, and the dollar was down over 3m. Policy rate -1.5 fits a rate near zero. Core CPI -1.5 also fits. I choose mid-2009, around June.

Note 1m equity returns are -0.5, which fits June 2009 (S&P roughly flat, +0.2%). Gold -1.0 over 1m also fits (it fell in June 2009).
